Subject: Production traffic blackhole — us-east-2 / Northshore

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing elevated 5xx rates and large latency spikes from ~08:50 PDT in our US-East-2 deployment behind Redwood. A subset of requests are now failing immediately (connection resets) and other requests are timing out after 10s. This began abruptly; our app team reports downstream retries are amplifying the load.

Attached is a screenshot of the error spike and a brief pod-state export. Support ticket NS-5012 created (link below). This is P0 for us — many patients-facing calls are affected.

Can you confirm if there is a regional issue on your side, and whether you can immediately reroute traffic away from the affected AZ while you investigate? We need a short-term routing diversion and an ETA for a fix.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Sr. SRE, Northshore Health
ops@northshore.health

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We're seeing the same signal in our edge telemetry (elevated 502/504 and connection resets from one AZ).

Immediate actions we are taking now:
- Activate rapid bridge: divert new sessions from the affected AZ to healthy AZs in the same region while we probe the root cause.
- Enable prefix caching for Northshore to reduce backend load during the diversion.
- Rishi is pulling kernel and network path logs; Hannah will monitor customer-facing dashboards and B2B SLA metrics.

We will confirm once the diversion is active (~10 min). Please keep the hubspot ticket updated with any changes on your side. I'll loop in Vanessa for cross-region authorization if we need to evacuate to a different region.

Kimberly Park

On Fri, Aug 28, 2026 at 09:31 Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We're seeing the same signal in our edge telemetry...

Quick technical update:
- Observed a sustained packet loss signature between AZ2 egress gateways and the internal inference fleet starting 08:48 PDT.
- Control plane remains reachable; KV cache hits are fine for warm-prefixes, but new session traffic shows multiple TCP resets and short-lived 5xx spikes.
- Initial pod logs show OOMKill spikes in the shard manager around 08:46 which correlate with autoscaler thrash on the node pool.

Plan (short horizon):
1) Force-divert traffic (edge) from AZ2 to AZ1/AZ3 within us-east-2 (5–12 min).
2) Suspend autoscaler for affected node pool to stop thrash.
3) Rehydrate prefix cache for Northshore after divert.

I'll publish kernel logs and a filtered stack trace to the incident link in ~15 minutes.

—Rishi
Tech Lead, Serving Runtime

- We will keep the diversion in place while Rishi completes a triage and we stabilize autoscaling.
- If traffic patterns normalize, we'll do a controlled reintroduce of AZ2 with a canary window and manual safety gates.

Please confirm if you're seeing improvement on your side and if you want us to keep the diversion in place for the next 2 hours while we complete validation.

Kimberly

Subject: Exec brief required — Northshore P0 (us-east-2 AZ2 isolation)

Team / Execs — raising for visibility and support: Northshore (key healthcare customer) experienced an AZ isolation event in us-east-2 (AZ2) starting 08:48 PDT. We activated an edge diversion at ~09:47 PDT which reduced customer 5xx by ~70% and restored most traffic. Rishi's triage shows node-pool autoscaler thrash that produced OOM/kill cascades and degraded egress from AZ2; we are treating root cause as infra autoscaler + transient network congestion.

Current status (14:03 PDT):
- Diversion: active, steady-state in AZ1/3.
- Customer impact: majority resolved; small percentage of long-tail requests still timing out.
- Estimated remediation ETA: 2–4 hours for controlled reintroduce and validation, or sooner if kernel patches and autoscaler policy hold.

Asks from CS/Ops:
- Execs: please approve an extended diversion window and priority runway for any emergency scaling or node replacement if Rishi requests it. This may require temporary capacity reallocation from our Dedicated pool (estimate: 12 GPU-mins/hour for 2 hours).
- Vanessa: please confirm we have authorization to escalate to cross-region failover if reintroduce attempts fail.

I'll keep Sara and Northshore updated on the next major milestone (canary reintroduce).

Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
